悪魔城ドラキュラ月下ライクなメトロイドヴァニア
古いと言うコメントもあるが、これはこれで一つのジャンルとしてあって良いと思う。
大切なのは中身の方で、キャラとシナリオ・戦闘と操作性・ボリュームと世界観。

キャラシナリオは日本のゲームではないので多少の違和感と同性愛的な押しが残念だけど、おおまかな流れは時間改変ものとしては王道な作りだと思う。個人的には5段階なら2くらいの印象。

戦闘と操作性は、まず難易度のバランスが良い。ソウルライクではないので簡単ではあるのだが、本家月下よりは手ごたえがあって良かった。
攻撃もオーブと必殺技の使い分けも良く、使い魔的なものもいるので◎
移動は快適になるスキルも覚えるし、ファストトラベルの数も申し分ない。
ただ時間を止めるのはあまり使用せず、戦闘だと使いにくいところはあるかもしれない。
大型ボスがいなかったので、そこも少し物足りなかったが、動きは丁寧な作りで5段階で4となった。

ボリュームと世界は、かなり控えめに感じた。その分2周目などはやりやすいかも。
世界も月下ほどのステージのインパクトはなく、過去と未来でもう少し違いが出ても良かったように思う。
ステージの多様性が欲しかったところ。ここは5段階で3。

総じて月下ライクなゲームがやりたい人には短めでオススメ出来ると言っても良いと思いました。

Like, they seemingly hired Dracula's interior decorator, architect, composer, and several of his bodyguards. But... it does a really good JOB of ripping off one of the best Metroidvanias ever, and the pixelart is gorgeous. I'm generally rather negative on pixelart, but this? This is GOOD.

I was gonna call it a solid 7/10, good value for what you're likely to pay for it these days, but then I finished it and... well, I've seen two of the three endings so far, and they were both AWESOME, feeling very much like a proper, cathargic reward for all your hard work. Those alone shot it up to an 8/10 for me. If you like Metroidvanias at all, you're probably gonna like this one, and it won't be a huge investment of money OR time, so give it a go!

I actually wish I had played this game sooner; it's been sitting on my backlog for... a while. But it's genuinely good, and I really enjoyed it! 

Overall the vibe is a contemporary / refined version of the late 16bit era to the best of 32bit era. The pixel art is gorgeous, the soundtrack is great, and kind of surprisingly, I really enjoyed the story. 

I do have a few small criticisms:

-The romances all felt super super forced. And while it wouldn't be worth noting otherwise, it sort of did take me out of the story. There is nothing wrong with romances mind you, but by the end of the game all the characters have paired off and none of them (including the MC) feel earned, or believable. 

-The writing between the MC and the main antagonist is also... off, which was surprising. It felt really out of place as well. Maybe the recurring theme here is the writer(s) struggled with writing interpersonal relationships, but excelled at worldbuilding.

-The game is a bit on the short side, and outside the last area, it's very very easy. Neither of these tarnish the game for me, but are worth noting. I do wish there was a little more tension in the exploration in terms of difficulty, but sometimes it's nice to have a chill, easy game to playthrough.

Overall, I'd definitely recommend it for fans of the genre or fans of 16bit/32bit style pixel art games.

Zuerst die (für mich) positiven Sachen:
- Mich hat sehr gefreut, dass dieses Metroidvania mehr auf der Seite von Castlevania als auf der von Metroid ist. Das heißt: Stats durch Level Ups und Equipment, Sidequests, ein Shop,  verschiedene Kampfstile durch verschiedene Waffen. Außerdem (verglichen mit vielen modernen Metroidvanias) gibt es quasi keine brutalen Gauntlets voller Gegner oder Stellen, wo man alle möglichen Skills aneinanderreihen muss um durch enge Korridore voller Stacheln zu kommen.
Mir macht diese Form von Metroidvania einfach so viel mehr Spaß.
- fantastischer Soundtrack
- tolles Pixelart
- angenehmes Movement
- eine Waffe toller als die letzte, mit tollen Fähigkeiten

Nun zur Kritik:
- Wenn im Orb-Menü direkt angezeigt werden würde, welche Schadensart (per Symbol) der ausgewählte Orb macht, wäre das sehr hilfreich. Einfach die gleichen Symbole wie im Enemy-Journal verwenden.
- Ich fand es sehr seltsam, dass unsere Protagonistin nie etwas zu den gefundenen Briefen oder Erinnerungen gesagt hat, weil diese ihre Vergangenheit ja maßgeblich aufdecken und sie beeinflussen sollten.
- Alles in allem war das Spiel doch sehr kurz. Ich verstehe zwar, dass es ein gigantischer Aufwand ist, all die Waffen, Animationen, Orte, Gegner und so weiter zu erstellen und einzubauen, aber irgendwie kam es mir (rein von der Dauer) nur wie ein halbes Spiel vor. Man beachte, dass meine Spielzeit einmal New Game und einmal New Game+ beinhaltet - also quasi eineinhalb Durchgänge. Trotzdem hatte ich enorm viel Spaß und bin sehr auf den kommenden, zweiten Teil gespannt!

Umm wow, I beat the game in less than 4 hours. I thought there was way more to do.

Besides being short, the gameplay is very lackluster. Just by playing the game naturally, you become so overleveled that the game is a cake walk. Most bosses can be killed on the first try and don't really have complex move sets. The level design is very bland. The amount of long corridors with the same enemy copy pasted every 20 feet is kinda crazy. 

You've got your generic cookie-cutter side quests asking you to "Fetch X items" or "Kill Y enemies". The rewards are also very lackluster. You also get a crazy amount of currency through natural gameplay with nothing useful to really spend it on, so currency is essentially worthless

Dialogue is written like something I would have written in 5th grade so I just started skipping it. 

The whole time freeze mechanic is barely utilized that you almost forget it's there, and when you do it trivializes the already easy combat even more. Just pause time and casually walk behind an enemy. No need to perfect dodge or place yourself strategically during combat. On top of this, there are platforming sections that _require_ you to time freeze to step on an enemy to reach higher ground, so if you kill that enemy, you have to leave and come back. If you're out of sand (time freeze resource) then you have to grind for that as well. Absurd design choice.

There are much better metroidvanias out there for the same price with astronomically more content

The art and music was good though

Ce jeu est excellent. C'est simple : c'est Castlevania, mais dans un univers de SF vraiment bien foutu et avec une difficulté beaucoup plus abordable. Les graphismes et les musiques sont sublimes. Le gameplay paraît basique au début, mais il fait le taff et, très vite, on a un nombre important de choix de personnalisation des capacités de combat qui rend le tout très agréable.

L'histoire est juste géniale. J'adore les histoires de voyage dans le temps, et là, je trouve que ça rend vraiment bien. Au début, on pense que l'histoire n'est qu'un prétexte et le voyage dans le temps un gadget, mais au bout d'un moment, ça devient vraiment génial.

Je reprocherais quand même que le délire ne va pas assez loin. Je trouve que les modifications que l'on fait dans le passé ne se voient pas suffisamment dans le futur. Ça aurait été bien de nous montrer que nos actions affaiblissent l'Empire plutôt que de nous le dire, parce qu'en l'état, on se demande comment notre personnage sait que ses actions ont une influence sur l'Empire dans le futur. Perso je ne vois pas le lien entre ce que notre personage voit autour de la statue et un afaiblissement de l'empire. Par exemple, les dev aurait pu mettre des soldats en arrière-plan dont le nombre diminue, ou des technologies moins impressionnantes. Mais j'ai déjà été très satisfait par ce qui se produit lorsque l'on détruit le portail."

Timespinner really is quite special. Even if every idea isn't fully-baked.

It's a search action/mapformer/metroidvania (delete as appropriate) in the Iga tradition, which is to say it resembles Symphony of the night, with a fun time gimmick to present 2(and a bit) maps to explore. Your weapons are a variety of magic orbs that produce effects from blunt force to lightning bolts to Star Platinum fists to guns. There are side quests, though not that many.

For non-completionists this'll run you 8 hours of solid exploration, which is plenty for me, and you get good enemy designs, music, and visuals as you go. That's all it had to do.

There's some additional stuff in levelling up your weapons and familiars, but in both cases you're likely to find a fave and stick with it (mine were the little dragon you get and the moon-based shattered orbs), which makes the levelling mechanics feel a bit basic outside of new game+.

I feel like I'm being a bit matter of fact, but this really is quite great. It's just that the stuff worth talking about is very mechanical. The story is fine, and the characters are likeable and inclusive. You get a couple of choices later on, even though they're basically all doable before you're done. It's good stuff. You just might not be inspired to shout from the roofs about it.

I will, however, be eager to follow these developers. Four stars.

O jogo é claramente uma homenagem direta a Castlevania Synphony of the Night. Este é um grande ponto positivo, me senti jogando uma continuação muito bem feita do jogo. Diversão, jogabilidade, progressão, é um trabalho impecável e primoroso. A trilha sonora extremamente bem feita de muito bom gosto, um trabalho magnífico e para um grande fã de Castlevania, foi uma grande satisfação ver design de personagens, jogabilidade e diversão e uma trilha sonora tão rica, bonita e bem feita. Parabéns à todos os envolvidos, estes são os pontos positivos do jogo que não poderia deixar de ressaltar de forma alguma. 
Tudo isso é destruído pela metade, praticamente, pela narrativa cansativa, história rasa, medíocre e sem graça.  É notório, claro e "empurrado" a visão progressista e feminista na história onde personagens masculinos são fracos, idiotas e entupidos de estrogênio, incapazes, comandados, subestimados e secundários. Para a narrativa e contexto, são totalmente descartáveis, inúteis e nem mesmo as quests deles não fazem a menor diferença em progressão ou impacto narrativo. Realmente lastimável, descartável e grosseiro. 
Absolutamente nada contra heroínas, nada contra grandes mulheres protagonistas mas a falta de respeito com o masculino, o descaso, o desdém e a repulsa que o roteiro do jogo demonstra chega a ser um insulto com jogadores homens. Realmente muito triste. Particularmente acredito que jogadoras, mulheres, caso não detenham em si pautas ideológicas de extrema esquerda, podem se sentir incomodadas e até mesmo, porque não dizer, insultadas, por não haver um par romântico que se prese, uma narrativa que valorize o feminino e seus atributos, que são tão bonitos e cheios de riqueza. 
Não acredito que este roteiro e história também agrade o público LGBTQIA+ (espero ter escrito da forma correta) pois as relações ♥♥♥♥ afetivas na história também são rasas, de difícil entendimento devido à confusões de roteiro e o distanciamento (para fins dramáticos) que o roteiro propõe. 
O casal gay principal do jogo é confuso, com conflitos de baixíssima relevância. Sinto pesar pois acredito que o público de nossos amigos LGBTQIA+ poderiam ter sido representados com mais carinho.
Enfim. Se a opção for jogar por jogar, pra se divertir com jogabilidade, desafio, grandes e longas sessões de bom combate e parkour satisfatório, recomento 100%. Mas para quem gosta de uma boa história, sinto muito mas existem jogos mais baratos, de desenvolvedores menores, com menos recursos que dispuseram produtos infinitamente melhores e mais satisfatórios no mercado. 
Acredito que o estúdio desenvolvedor tem um potencial enorme e faço votos de que tenham muito sucesso e façam mais e mais jogos tão bem feitos e bem produzidos quanto, pois jogar foi uma experiência incrível. Mas manter os roteiristas e responsáveis pela narrativa é um erro fatal e a prova disso são os inúmeros estúdios que fecharam, líderes demitidos e investidores cortando verbas. Vide a Disney.
Bem, sucesso aos desenvolvedores mas eu adoraria ter uma opinião diferente. O jogo é realmente lindo e muito divertido mas não recomendo, e principalmente, para pais que querem presentear seus filhos.

Despite an absolutely everywhere story when you read all the side content, Timespinner is pretty good. I liked it mostly for it's gameplay.
Overall, this game is an love letter to the Castlevania series mechanically. You have 2 "hands" to attack with like Order of Ecclesia, but now both tied to one attack button. You have a special, more powerful attack that charges up and requires an automatically recharging MP bar like Charlotte from Portrait of Ruin. You also have a passive equipment slot for special bonuses to your weapons at all times, akin to Aria/Dawn of Sorrow. You have a somewhat handy backdash as well, like most Castlevania Metroidvania titles. You even get a range of familiars like Symphony of the Night, but I only ever tried out the first one because it's extraordinarily tedious to them up. They're not very useful even after being leveled, sadly.
I won't go too much into the story, as it's a cheesy, fantasy, sci-fi time-travel story. But, the time travel elements of the story, and sometimes in gameplay, let you effect the world in ways akin to Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance, where actions in one castle effect the other castle. In Timespinner, though, it is, of course, things that happen in the past effecting the future.
Finally, I do want to mention the very inspired, yet beautiful soundtrack. It's highly reminiscent of, yes, Castlevania games like Order of Ecclesia or Symphony of the Night, but the tracks are distinct and awesome in their own way. The instrumentation is just pristine.
It took me about 12 hours to 100% while taking my time, not at all a bad Metroidvania experience.
